# Batch partition and first offset in each aggregate for safe re-writes

> Each minute-click aggregate records the Kafka batch's partition and first offset, enabling safe re-delivery without duplicates.

_Part of [Exactly-once Kafka transaction for aggregates and offsets](exactly-once-transaction.md)_

When click records from a Kafka batch are aggregated into per-minute totals by campaign, the [`aggregateBatch`](ad-click-aggregation-and-billing.md) function tags each aggregate with two pieces of batch identity: the `source_partition` (which partition the batch came from) and the `first_offset` (the offset of the first message in the batch). If the Kafka transaction fails and aborts, the batch is re-read from the same starting offset, producing the same aggregates with the same tags. Downstream consumers use (campaign, minute, partition, `first_offset`) as the unique key for these aggregates, so a re-delivered aggregate replaces the prior one instead of creating a duplicate. This is how [exactly-once delivery](exactly-once-transaction.md) is achieved.

**Look at:** [`MinuteAggregate` in click-aggregator.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/infra/click-aggregator.service.ts#L11) · [`aggregateBatch` in click-aggregator.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/infra/click-aggregator.service.ts#L21)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| queue | `ads.clicks` | Input Kafka topic; each message is a [`ClickRecord`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) to aggregate |
| queue | `ads.click-aggregates` | Output Kafka topic; each message is a [`MinuteAggregate`](ad-click-aggregation-and-billing.md) with partition and offset |

## Watch out

- The `first_offset` is the batch's first message offset, not the last. The consumer group's committed offset points one-past-the-last message, which is where the next poll resumes from.
- Downstream must use (campaign, minute, partition, `first_offset`) as the unique key; a naive merge on just (campaign, minute) would see duplicates on re-delivery.
- Re-delivery only happens if the producer transaction aborts; if the consumer crashes after the transaction commits, the batch is not re-read.
- A single batch may aggregate to multiple (campaign, minute) combinations, but all aggregates from that batch have the same partition and `first_offset`.
